correctness.rationale: For any cover, select one cyclic occurrence of each of 32 distinct length-nine palindromes; successive start separations dominate their minimum overlap shifts. The explicit integer potentials sum to 81 and all 496 unordered pair costs have only seven positive deficits totaling 20, hence any covering circle has length at least 2*81-20=142. A 142-bit linear word contains all 32 palindromes. Two self-contained checkers recompute the complete cost certificate independently, one with literal strings and one with integer masks. A linear cover is also a cyclic cover of the same length.

value.rationale: This closes a specific outstanding exact finite-length minimum for the natural all-palindromes shortest-superstring family tracked in a public sequence. The proof is a small, reproducible combinatorial dual certificate, not just a repeated greedy construction or routine number-table computation; the same certificate establishes both linear and circular optimal lengths. No broader theorem is needed to make the exact ninth-order cutoff relevant.
